reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because the speaker directly promotes Forsage as a way to obtain passive income, including money arriving while the viewer is sleeping, and urges immediate participation because it is supposedly growing rapidly. He tells viewers to click the link and says they can purchase or fund a position, so the video combines an income promise with a participation and diversion pathway rather than merely discussing cryptocurrency.

opening.argument: Judge the speaker's market outlook by what he actually says: growth is anticipated, not guaranteed. His forecast is framed as an expectation about cryptocurrency over the next 12 to 24 months, and his invitation is conditional on the viewer's interest. He offers to provide information, which leaves room for the viewer to assess the opportunity. His confidence and urgency deserve scrutiny, but neither converts an explicitly prospective market view into a guaranteed return.

citations.quote: It's anticipated that it's going to grow a tremendous amount in this next 12 to 24 months
if you're interested at it all in the Forsage business in the cryptocurrencies and coins and all of that sort of thing just click the link below and let me know and we'll get you some information

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening fairly identifies the speaker's enthusiasm, but its quoted income language describes what a viewer might want; it does not specify an amount or guarantee a payment. Likewise, the quoted invitation to visit a site says the viewer can find out more. Those passages support concern about promotion, not a conclusion that a particular return has been promised.

citations.quote: Especially if you want passive income and want to have money coming when you're sleeping, when you're not working
Just go to Crypto4the the ages.com and you'll find out what it's all about

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A conditional market forecast does not neutralize the video's separate pitch. The speaker urges viewers to act immediately and connects participation to passive income arriving while they sleep. He also describes purchasing or funding a position. The issue is not whether he specifies a guaranteed amount; it is that he solicits participation in an income opportunity.

opening.argument: There is an operational explanation here, not just an income claim. The speaker describes transactions reaching a crypto wallet and says the process runs on the blockchain; the description identifies Ethereum smart contracts. A judge can read the invitation to find out more as a pointer to information about how the platform works. These explanations do not verify the system, but they give the video a technology-focused reading beyond the most promotional lines.

citations.quote: it goes to immediately to your Crypto wallet nobody else handles your money It's all on the blockchain it all works automatically
Forsage is a new way of transacting on the blockchain using Ethereum Smart Contracts
Just go to Crypto4the the ages.com and you'll find out what it's all about

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference opening treats the purchase of a position as decisive, but the speaker also describes where transactions go and who handles the money. The quote about a position, standing alone, does not establish the payout rules or demonstrate that money is being diverted. The operational claims may be unverified, yet explaining those claims is part of what the video does.

You control your money every Time a Transaction take place That comes to you it goes to immediately to your Crypto wallet nobody else handles your money

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The technical vocabulary does not make this an operational tutorial. The speaker gives no demonstrated procedure for inspecting a contract or verifying a transaction. Instead, he couples his account of the platform with an invitation to join, an urgent call to act and the prospect of passive income. The cited wallet claims are part of his sales pitch, not independent evidence that the opportunity works as described.

opening.argument: The visible transaction the speaker describes is funding a position on a crowdfunding platform, with payments going to a crypto wallet. He does not specify a fixed yield, a repayment schedule, a required downline or a request for credentials in this account. The judge should not infer those missing mechanics from the word 'position' alone. The stronger narrow reading is an enthusiastic promotion of a blockchain-based service whose actual terms are not established by this video.

you simply purchase a position or fund a position however you want to put it
Forsage is a new way of transacting on the blockchain using Ethereum Smart Contracts

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference opening establishes a pitch for income and participation, but its quoted request to visit the site is a request to learn more, not a credential request or a displayed payment instruction. Nor does the cited purchase language explain how any returns are generated. Promotion alone does not settle whether the underlying transaction is an ordinary service purchase or a deceptive income scheme.

citations.quote: Just go to Crypto4the the ages.com and you'll find out what it's all about
you simply purchase a position or fund a position however you want to put it

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Missing a fixed rate or credential request does not turn this into ordinary commerce. The speaker explicitly ties the funded position to receiving money when not working and urges viewers to join now. That combination is an income-opportunity solicitation; the absence of detailed payout rules limits what can be said about its mechanics, not what the video is promoting.
